title: Synergy of strength–ductility in HfMoTaTiZr refractory high entropy alloy through Cr addition

recollection.starting_material: HfMoTaTiZr refractory high entropy alloy (likely a BCC single-phase solid solution)
recollection.intervention: Addition of Chromium (Cr) as a minor alloying element (guess: likely in the range of 5-15 at.%)
recollection.structure: A modified BCC solid solution structure, potentially with the formation of a secondary phase (e.g., sigma phase or Laves phase) or a refined grain structure due to Cr addition (guess)
recollection.mechanism: Synergistic strengthening and ductility enhancement via solid solution strengthening, grain boundary strengthening, and potentially transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) or twinning-induced plasticity (TWIP) effects, or suppression of brittle phases (guess)
recollection.results: Significant improvement in both yield strength and total elongation compared to the base HfMoTaTiZr alloy, achieving a strength-ductility synergy (e.g., yield strength > 800 MPa and elongation > 15%, or similar high values) (guess)

score.note: Correctly identifies Cr addition, but the amount is only a broad guess and misses the actual 4.2 at.%. It tentatively mentions a Laves phase in a BCC matrix, but does not identify the reticulated Cr2(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) network. Solid-solution strengthening is correctly suggested, while the key crack-hindrance/plasticity-compensation mechanism is missed and several unsupported mechanisms are proposed. The estimated strength is far below 1750.6 MPa, the elongation is not close to 14.0%, and hardness and Laves-phase fraction are absent.
